html:
SMTO-TSK-0044 — This step was skipped because the task was stopped

GUID: 5d8fd59f-aaea-4b69-b67c-5cfda8c85fde
Slug: run-cancelled
Domain: TSK · Subsystem: tsk

What happened

  • The task was stopped before this step began, so the step never ran and changed nothing. Steps that finished before the stop keep their results.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the task and look at its status and at the results of steps that finished before it stopped. Earlier steps keep their results; only this step was skipped.
  2. If you or someone else stopped the task on purpose, you don't need to do anything else. This message only records that the step didn't run.
  3. If you didn't expect the task to stop, find out who stopped it, for example a Stop pressed in another window, before deciding what to do next. Knowing why it stopped helps you avoid running work nobody wanted.

What success looks like

  • The task shows as stopped or cancelled, and this step is listed as not run.

If it still fails

  • If the task stopped without anyone selecting Stop, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume the skipped step happened; it did not run.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The activity worker found the run or activity stop flag set before this activity started and recorded a cancelled, unexecuted result (executed=false, no remote effect possible).

What this means

  • The activity worker observes the run/activity stop flag before this activity starts and creates a cancelled unexecuted rejection. Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.

Why this can happen

  • The activity worker observes the run/activity stop flag before this activity starts and creates a cancelled unexecuted rejection.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect this activity's unstarted receipt separately from earlier activities that may have completed.

How to fix it

  • No corrective action is required for this informational outcome.
  • No fix is required; this is an informational unexecuted receipt for one activity. Inspect the run status and earlier activity results separately, and do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Retry and execution caution

  • This state requests no new execution or automatic retry. Inspect the current task controls and retained results.

How to verify the fix

  • The activity remains unexecuted and earlier work retains its own results.

What not to do

  • Do not turn this status into an automatic retry or a new execution request.

Technical notes

  • Task state and retained ownership decide whether an action is eligible. Diagnostics do not change lane order, consent, snapshots, cancellation or execution; preserve original receipts and reconcile any possible effects before new work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
